podcast.body: Written by founding member Graham Goble, inspired by a C9 chord shown to him by David Briggs, this song was released in June 1978 on the *Sleeper Catcher* album. It peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot 100 in the US and garnered high praise from John Lennon, who listened to it "on repeat," and Frank Sinatra. Goble attributed its greater popularity in the US compared to Australia to its depiction of "the world that was my internal world," a fantasy of 1940s and 1950s American pop culture that resonated strongly with Americans raised in that era. The record label initially overlooked its potential as a single. "All that is not exactly what's it's my it though it was written by gobel it was inspired by a chord that David Briggs showed him it was simply from that chord and it's a C9 for those who care about that sort of thing that these lyrics and melody float."
